## A1-0726 — Keep explicit computation separate from instrumentId-based stitch-and-upload

**Source stance:** requested-change

**Context:**

> component: marketdata-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/marketdata/impl/managers/StitchMonthlyChangesManager.scala; operation: Feat/INV-4918 stitch data fields; trigger: Source-specific review condition as stated in the exact comment below.

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Yea this looks wrong, in term API design, let’s stay with prev implementation:
> 
> * compute with explicit request: only compute, using stitch config from request payload
> * stitch: change to take only instrumentId \(i.e. fetch stitch config from instrument, no more request payload\), support simulationOnly \+ forceOverride flag \(in case contradicting existing data\)
> 
> Keep `StitchMonthlyChangesManager` strictly about computation as before, no need to pollute it with upload \(or not\) logic
> 
> Use cases:
> 
> * on instrument created: stitch && simulation = false && override = false
> * on stitch config updated \(called by instrument svc\): stitch && simulation = false && override = true \(if we are worried about unintentional update causing unexpected data change, we can stay with override = false first & error to alert the inconsistency instead\)
> * on system endpoint call \(e.g. monthly cron\): stitch && simulation = false && override = false
> * on manual endpoint call: either compute or stitch, with any flags, up to caller
> 
> ‌

**Conditions and limits:**

- Context component is inline_path metadata; operation is the exact PR title quoted separately from comment evidence.
- Preserve trigger matrix, simulate/force flags, and alternative error-on-config-change; StitchMonthlyChangesManager stays computation only.

> * However, we have 2 problems:

This means if user selects B2B group portfolio, the endpoint returns None, and once again errors are repeated due to retries. >

## A1-0822 — Slick insert projection takes EventTagRecordInput and returns generated ordering

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> component: akka-abstraction-layer/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/projection/auto/AutoProjectionEventSourceProvider.scala; operation: [NE-363] introduce auto projection; trigger: Source-specific review condition as stated in the exact comment below.

**Concern stated in the source:** Normal records always have required ordering, eliminating optional checks

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Maybe something like this
> 
> ```
> case class EventTagRecordInput(...other fields...)
> 
> case class EventTagRecord(
>   ordering: Long,
>   ...other fields...
> )
> 
> object EventTagRecord {
>   def fromInput(input: EventTagRecordInput, ordering: Long): EventTagRecord = ...
> }
> ```
> 
> ‌
> 
> Table with proper required auto-incrementing PK
> 
> ```
> class EventTagTable {
> 
>   def ordering: Rep[Long] = column[Long]("ordering", O.PrimaryKey, O.AutoInc)
>   ...other columns...
> 
>   override def * : ProvenShape[EventTagRecord] =
>     (ordering, persistenceId, eventManifest, event, tag, addedAt).<>((EventTagRecord.apply _).tupled, EventTagRecord.unapply)
> 
>   def projectionForInsert =
>     (persistenceId, eventManifest, event, tag, addedAt).<>((EventTagRecordInput.apply _).tupled, EventTagRecordInput.unapply)
> }
> ```
> 
> ‌
> 
> ```
> trait EventTagDao {
>   def insert(item: EventTagRecordInput): Future[Long]
>   def readNext(n: Long)(tag: String, from: Long): Future[List[EventTagRecord]]
> }
> ```
> 
> ‌
> 
> ```
> class EventTagDaoJdbc extends EventTagDao {
>   def insert(item: EventTagRecordInput): Future[Long] = {
>     val insertQuery = table
>       .map(_.projectionForInsert)
>       .returning(table.map(_.ordering))
>       .into(EventTagRecord.fromInput)
> 
>     db.run(insertQuery += item).map(_.ordering)
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> ‌
> 
> Then in every usage of EventTagRecord, we have proper required `ordering` field instead of having to check optional.

## A1-0868 — Standalone model separates automatic attributes from forced override and early deeplink validation

**Source stance:** explanation

**Context:**

> component: None; operation: [INV-4869] feat(bff, advisory, instrument, portfolio): Add a flag for instruments which are marked as Standalone-only and add amount restriction in fund-smart invest flow summary; trigger: Source-specific review condition as stated in the exact comment below.

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Just to summarize a bit so that we’re on the same page.
> 
> ‌
> 
> We have 2 levels of logic to determine if a fund is a standalone fund:
> 
> * derived logic based on fund attributes \(i.e. semi-liquid, redemption regulations, lots size, non-daily schedule\)… these are “rules” to auto qualify funds as standalone, without Ops having to configure anything
> * a “forced” flag to explicitly set a fund as standalone, even if they don’t check any of the above boxes… e.g. large NAV funds
> 
>   
> On `InstrumentInfoDto` \(static configuration of instrument data\), as of current PR, FE will only see the forced flag, but not the derived one. Hence on advisory instrument-list / instrument-details endpoints, BE would resolve both of the above and send a single resolved flag to FE to tell if a fund is effectively a standalone or not. This way FE can implement UX logic to guide customer for fund selection, so all that is good.
> 
> ‌
> 
> If customer lands on a deeplink with TAA to portfolio summary screen \(i.e. bypassing FE guardrails on fund selection\), we need to tell FE if such TAA is valid or not:
> 
> * if we handle everything properly, we would need to return it as warning/block flags at instrument level, so that FE can display properly \(similar to HK\)
> * but since we agreed to descope this piece \(i.e. no FE display\), we want to ensure at least such request is blocked as early as possible, not allowing customer to continue all the way to OTP and then get 5xx error
> 
> This eager block can be a simple flag in portfolio summary response, and FE can handle \(error or proper failure popup with explanation\). Or we can go with generic BadRequest as well. This is up to yall to discuss.
> 
> ‌
> 
> Another approach is to serialize the resolved isStandaloneFund flag in `InstrumentInfoDto` as a derived field as well \(i.e. not part of constructors, no setter, but part of json\). Then we leave it completely to FE to check the individual instruments' flag and handle.

**Conditions and limits:**

- Context component is inline_path metadata; operation is the exact PR title quoted separately from comment evidence.
- Derived semi-liquid, redemption regulation, lot size, nondaily schedule; early flag/BadRequest or JSON-only derived InstrumentInfoDto field proposed; OTP-late 5xx unacceptable.

## A1-1407 — Do not use missing CPF/SRS firm fee config as FE toggle

> component: None; operation: Feat/BB-2642 bff retrive cpf srs fee detail; trigger: Source-specific review condition as stated in the exact comment below.

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Fee range must be configured for all trading accounts at the point of firm onboarding. Missing config for CPF/SRS should be treated as data/setup issue, and we must not use it as FE feature toggle.
> 
> * Linking/displaying account should be supported regardless of existence of fee range config
> * Add goal flow can be changed to fail instead of fallback to empty fee range, so that FA can escalate
> 
> ‌
> 
> Moreover, current impl is too fragile:
> 
> * Data is returned in full shape. Should a customer be able to view such config of the firm, even if they belongs to same firm?
> * No RBAC / No ownership guards: once authenticated, anyone can call the endpoint by providing a customerId. Think customer/fa of Firm X calling the endpoint with customerId of Firm Y
> 
> ‌
> 
> We shouldn’t need this endpoint for this purpose of show/hide CPF/SRS features in FE \(at least not driven by missing data\).
> 
> If any, this endpoint is only useful when we want to display/manage firm’s fee range config in Advisor Portal, by PartnerOps or some super-FAM \(as opposed to manually controlled by Endowus Ops\)
> 
> When such requirement comes, we would still need proper RBAC resource for this tenant level data \+ new CanActionForTenantGuard
> 
> CC

> 
> ```
> /pending-approvals/creator/:creatorId?assigneeRole
> /pending-approvals/assignee/:assigneeId
> ```
> 
> ‌
> 
> BFF
> 
> ```
> A. my-created-and-pending-manager-requests/taskType/:taskType
> - calls /pending-approvals/creator/<authenticated-employeeId>?assigneeRole=FA_MANAGER
> - RBAC: Create action for RBAC resource coresponding to taskType
> 
> B. my-created-and-pending-client-requests/taskType/:taskType
> - calls /pending-approvals/creator/<authenticated-employeeId>?assigneeRole=CLIENT
> - RBAC: Create action for RBAC resource coresponding to taskType
> 
> C. pending-my-approval/taskType/:taskType
> - calls /pending-approvals/assignee/<authenticated-employeeId/customerId>
> - RBAC: Approve action for RBAC resource coresponding to taskType
> ```
> 
> ‌
> 
> BFF currently splits advisor-portal \(AdvisorPortal\*\) and client-portal \(SilverFe\*\). This means \(C\) needs to be duplicated.
> 
> BFF will eventually unify the FE clients \(every endpoint need to support all user types, as long as they pass the RBAC and guards validation\)

**Conditions and limits:**

- Keep the three concrete route/RBAC mappings from the source; pending-my-approval is duplicated until client unification.

## A2-0282 — PlanFeeInstructionEntity: The entity state is default with empty fee instructions, it means the plan always exists, just without any data. Modelling it this way means you can’t ...

**Source stance:** open-question

**Context:**

> PR 10030 ([EN-3952] (charge) Create new PlanFeeInstructionEntity), charge-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/charge/impl/entities/instruction/PlanFeeInstructionEntity.scala; original row 282.

**Concern stated in the source:** Empty default instructions cannot distinguish never-initialized from upserted-then-deleted plan state.

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> The entity state is default with empty fee instructions, it means the plan always exists, just without any data. Modelling it this way means you can’t distinguish between a uninitialized plan vs a plan with upserted-then-deleted fee instructions.
> 
> If we care enough about this, then we probably should make state a sealed trait, default with case object NotInitialized, otherwise it’s case class Initialized\(feeInstructions\). Then you can throw for GetCmd/DeleteCmd on NotInitialized. And no-op without error if deleting already deleted fee instruction for Initialized, and even throw if deleting last entry for Initialized \(to ensure there’s always an entry to support the fee rate query\)

**Conditions and limits:**

- The sealed NotInitialized/Initialized state is conditional on caring about that distinction; no-op deletion and last-entry rejection are proposals within that model.
- PR title and inline path identify source component/operation context only; quoted PR title is metadata, not a claim that the comment proposal was implemented.

## A2-0434 — Review: I think we should:

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 10262 (Feat/INV-3637 bff endpoint upload document), no inline path; original row 434.

**Concern stated in the source:** Document upload has no customer context, whereas GET must verify customer/context ownership in the domain edge service.

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> I think we should:
> 
> * create new endpoint in document svc `/api/v1/document/upload` with this UploadDocumentRequest type \(maybe optional documentId if there is need to control this id from caller\), and its logic calls `createDocumentWithBinaries` providing the OTHERS value for the deprecated enums
> * create authenticated endpoint in BFF proxy to above endpoint in document svc, for advisor portal, ~~which requires \(CUSTOMER:DOCUMENT resource & Create permission\)~~
> * do not allow for client portal for now, since there is no planned flow that requires this yet
> 
> ‌
> 
> Later on when we add GET endpoints, then it will be applicable for both advisor portal and client portal, ~~both require \(CUSTOMER:DOCUMENT resource & Read permission\)~~
> 
> Unlike the POST upload endpoint which doesn’t care about the context of document, the GET ones must care and validate the document indeed belongs to the customer \+ context. Hence these GET endpoints will have to be edge in the context service, e.g. goal/customer svc instead of direct document svc. This means these services would be responsible to capture the generated documentId from the upload endpoint.
> 
> ‌
> 
> Example for add goal flow:
> 
> * FA uploads document in advisor-portal → calls BFF to proxy to document svc → advisor-portal captures generated documentId
> * FA confirms to create the add-goal approval request in advisor-portal → calls BFF to proxy to advisory svc, which eventually creates workflow in workflow-engine
> 
>     * The workflow request must contain all the documentIds associated with this add-goal request
>     
> * When workflow request is fully approved → workflow-engine calls advisory svc which calls goal svc to create goal
> 
>     * We need to somehow persist these documentIds to the goalId
>     
> * When customer retrieves suitability doc from goal page in client-portal → calls BFF to proxy to goal svc `GET /api/v1/goal/:goalId/document` or `GET /api/v1/goal/:goalId/document/:documentId`
> 
>     * BFF validates goalId belongs to customerId
>     * goal svc validates documentId belongs to goalId
>     
> 
> ‌

**Conditions and limits:**

- The CUSTOMER:DOCUMENT RBAC suggestions in this source comment are struck through and clarified in row 436; do not revive them as requirements for bare upload.

## A2-0469 — BffServiceImpl: In on-behalf operations:

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 10258 ([INV-3639] feat(bff): Capture and propagate Customer/Employee context in BFF), bff-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/bff/impl/BffServiceImpl.scala; original row 469.

**Concern stated in the source:** In on-behalf operations:

* auth user would be employee, which we would set into context using EmployeeProvider
* and the request \(either payload or query param\) should specify the customer, which we would use to validate proper ownership/relationship in guards

‌

Once it reaches the handler \(logic layer\), it is up to the domain to decide how they want to implement it. Example:

1. they could use an endpoint in BE that expects customerId in either payload or query param \(and hence we can simply reuse it completely, and define it as proxy endpoint in BFF\)
2. they could set context using CustomerProvider, and call the endpoint in BE that expects customerId from context instead \(and if not available, 500 error is rightfully thrown\)

I would prefer \(1\) instead and we stick to setting TenantId/CustomerId/EmployeeId context by auth only.

>

def handleUpdateProductCharacteristicsCmd(cmd: UpdateProductCharacteristicsCmd, state: GoalState): Reply = {
  cmd.newProductLineAndIntent match {
      case x: productline.B2CProductLineAndIntent =>
        handleUpdateB2CProductCharacteristicsCmd(cmd, state, x)
      case _: productline.B2BProductLineAndIntent =>
        Effect.reply(cmd.replyTo)(
          GoalSvcException("Invalid product line and intent, only supports B2C product lines", GoalSvcErrorType.???).error
        )
  }
}

## A2-0783 — SgRecommendedInvestmentManager: Best if we can refactor to avoid make unnecessary calls

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 9739 (Feat/EN-3683 sg create a new api to get recommended investment amount), advisory-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/advisory/impl/managers/sg/SgRecommendedInvestmentManager.scala; original row 783.

**Concern stated in the source:** Best if we can refactor to avoid make unnecessary calls

```
lazy val tierLevelFut = getCustomerIncomeTierLevel(customerId)
lazy val myInfoFinancialDataFut = getMyInfoFinancialData(customerId)

tradingAccountType match {
  case TradingAccountType.SINGAPORE_SGD_CASH_ACCOUNT =>
    tierLevelFut.map { level =>
      deriveRecommendationFromIncomeTier(level, RecommendedRecurringMonthlyAmountSgdCashBasedOnIncomeLevelMap)
    }

  case TradingAccountType.SINGAPORE_CPF_OA_ACCOUNT =>
    for {
      myInfoFinancialData <- myInfoFinancialDataFut
      response <- deriveRecommendationFromMyInfo(myInfoFinancialData) match {
        case Some(recommendation) =>
          Future.successful(recommendation)
        case None =>
          tierLevelFut.map { level =>
            deriveRecommendationFromIncomeTier(level, RecommendedRecurringMonthlyAmountCpfBasedOnIncomeLevelMap)
          }
      }
    } yield response

  case _ =>
    Future.successful(RecommendedInvestmentDto.noRecommendation())
}
```

‌

No need to split the helper methods too fine, especially when they are not used in more than one place

* `getCustomerIncomeTierLevel` can do both customer lookup and perform mapping to TierLevel
* `getMyInfoFinancialData` can do myinfo lookup, if found then return, else only then do onboarding lookup and perform mapping

‌

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Best if we can refactor to avoid make unnecessary calls
> 
> ```
> lazy val tierLevelFut = getCustomerIncomeTierLevel(customerId)
> lazy val myInfoFinancialDataFut = getMyInfoFinancialData(customerId)
> 
> tradingAccountType match {
>   case TradingAccountType.SINGAPORE_SGD_CASH_ACCOUNT =>
>     tierLevelFut.map { level =>
>       deriveRecommendationFromIncomeTier(level, RecommendedRecurringMonthlyAmountSgdCashBasedOnIncomeLevelMap)
>     }
> 
>   case TradingAccountType.SINGAPORE_CPF_OA_ACCOUNT =>
>     for {
>       myInfoFinancialData <- myInfoFinancialDataFut
>       response <- deriveRecommendationFromMyInfo(myInfoFinancialData) match {
>         case Some(recommendation) =>
>           Future.successful(recommendation)
>         case None =>
>           tierLevelFut.map { level =>
>             deriveRecommendationFromIncomeTier(level, RecommendedRecurringMonthlyAmountCpfBasedOnIncomeLevelMap)
>           }
>       }
>     } yield response
> 
>   case _ =>
>     Future.successful(RecommendedInvestmentDto.noRecommendation())
> }
> ```
> 
> ‌
> 
> No need to split the helper methods too fine, especially when they are not used in more than one place
> 
> * `getCustomerIncomeTierLevel` can do both customer lookup and perform mapping to TierLevel
> * `getMyInfoFinancialData` can do myinfo lookup, if found then return, else only then do onboarding lookup and perform mapping

## A2-0869 — PerformanceCalculator: Same same only, but I think structuring the logic this way makes it easier for me to visualize

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 9543 (Resolve INV-3136: Calculate max draw down for a given set of monthlyChanges.), performance-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/performance/impl/utils/PerformanceCalculator.scala; original row 869.

**Concern stated in the source:** Same same only, but I think structuring the logic this way makes it easier for me to visualize

```
var currentPeak, mddPeak, mddTrough = monthlyChanges.head
var maybeCurrentTrough: Option[MonthlyChange] = None
var maxDrawDown = BigDecimal(0)

def calculate(): Unit = {
  maybeCurrentTrough.foreach { currentTrough =>
    val drawDown = ((currentTrough.nav - currentPeak.nav) / currentPeak.nav).setScale(6, RoundingMode.HALF_EVEN)
    if (drawDown < maxDrawDown) {
      maxDrawDown = drawDown
      mddPeak = currentPeak
      mddTrough = currentTrough
    }
  }
  maybeCurrentTrough = None
}

for (current <- monthlyChanges) {
  if (current.nav > currentPeak.nav) {
    // Exiting current peak, attempt to calculate drawdown if already found current trough
    calculate()
    currentPeak = current
  } else if (maybeCurrentTrough.forall(_.nav > current.nav)) {
    // Not captured yet, or found new trough from current peak, just update
    maybeCurrentTrough = Some(current)
  }
}
// calculate for last peak
calculate()

Option.when(maxDrawDown < 0)(
  MaxDrawDown(drawDown = Math.abs(maxDrawDown.doubleValue()), peak = mddPeak, trough = mddTrough)
)
```

‌

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Same same only, but I think structuring the logic this way makes it easier for me to visualize
> 
> ```
> var currentPeak, mddPeak, mddTrough = monthlyChanges.head
> var maybeCurrentTrough: Option[MonthlyChange] = None
> var maxDrawDown = BigDecimal(0)
> 
> def calculate(): Unit = {
>   maybeCurrentTrough.foreach { currentTrough =>
>     val drawDown = ((currentTrough.nav - currentPeak.nav) / currentPeak.nav).setScale(6, RoundingMode.HALF_EVEN)
>     if (drawDown < maxDrawDown) {
>       maxDrawDown = drawDown
>       mddPeak = currentPeak
>       mddTrough = currentTrough
>     }
>   }
>   maybeCurrentTrough = None
> }
> 
> for (current <- monthlyChanges) {
>   if (current.nav > currentPeak.nav) {
>     // Exiting current peak, attempt to calculate drawdown if already found current trough
>     calculate()
>     currentPeak = current
>   } else if (maybeCurrentTrough.forall(_.nav > current.nav)) {
>     // Not captured yet, or found new trough from current peak, just update
>     maybeCurrentTrough = Some(current)
>   }
> }
> // calculate for last peak
> calculate()
> 
> Option.when(maxDrawDown < 0)(
>   MaxDrawDown(drawDown = Math.abs(maxDrawDown.doubleValue()), peak = mddPeak, trough = mddTrough)
> )
> ```
> 
> ‌

**Conditions and limits:**

- Proposed calculation keeps currentPeak/mddPeak/mddTrough, rounds negative drawdown to scale 6 HALF_EVEN, calculates when leaving a peak and once at the end, and returns None unless maxDrawDown<0.

## A2-0890 — HalfOfYear: Also there’s a general movement to use sealed trait \+ case object instead of `Enumeration` \(until we migrate to scala 3\) [<url> data-inline-card='' }

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 9240 ([INV-3011] feat(report): Generate semi annual report), silver-commons/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/commons/time/HalfOfYear.scala; original row 890.

**Concern stated in the source:** Also there’s a general movement to use sealed trait \+ case object instead of `Enumeration` \(until we migrate to scala 3\) [<url> data-inline-card='' }

Then we can even add methods for them. Examples

```
sealed trait HalfOfYear {
  def getStartDate(year: Int): LocalDate
  def getEndDate(year: Int): LocalDate
  def getEndYearMonth(year: Int): YearMonth
}
case object H1 extends HalfOfYear {
  def getStartDate(year: Int): LocalDate = LocalDate.of(year, 1, 1)
  def getEndDate(year: Int): LocalDate = LocalDate.of(year, 6, 30)
  def getEndYearMonth(year: Int): YearMonth = YearMonth.of(year, 6)
}
```

‌

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Also there’s a general movement to use sealed trait \+ case object instead of `Enumeration` \(until we migrate to scala 3\) [<url> data-inline-card='' }
> 
> Then we can even add methods for them. Examples
> 
> ```
> sealed trait HalfOfYear {
>   def getStartDate(year: Int): LocalDate
>   def getEndDate(year: Int): LocalDate
>   def getEndYearMonth(year: Int): YearMonth
> }
> case object H1 extends HalfOfYear {
>   def getStartDate(year: Int): LocalDate = LocalDate.of(year, 1, 1)
>   def getEndDate(year: Int): LocalDate = LocalDate.of(year, 6, 30)
>   def getEndYearMonth(year: Int): YearMonth = YearMonth.of(year, 6)
> }
> ```
> 
> ‌

**Conditions and limits:**

- Sealed trait/case object is a historical convention until Scala 3, illustrated with H1 Jan1–Jun30 and June YearMonth; do not universalize it into a permanent ban on Enumeration.

## A2-1081 — ReportApplication: Just some notes here, yall are right about the trade-offs but manual start is not that bad, depending on use cases.

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 9306 (Feat/EN-3405 use tasktopicsubscriber in report for manual start/stop), report-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/report/impl/ReportApplication.scala; original row 1081.

**Concern stated in the source:** Just some notes here, yall are right about the trade-offs but manual start is not that bad, depending on use cases.

In case of report, the svc itself is responsible for triggering of the topic producer side. So we can potentially just call start \(via distributed pubsub\) in the same trigger endpoint, i.e. `createMonthlyStatementsV2` first will trigger start, only then produce the message.

* the start is idempotent so if already started, it won’t cause any harm
* the distributed pubsub is at-most once tho, so it could still happen that maybe one of instance does not start… but I suppose this could be checked easily via logs or metrics.

‌

We can also make this pause/resume status persisted, and check upon startup :thumbsup: 

‌

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Just some notes here, yall are right about the trade-offs but manual start is not that bad, depending on use cases.
> 
> In case of report, the svc itself is responsible for triggering of the topic producer side. So we can potentially just call start \(via distributed pubsub\) in the same trigger endpoint, i.e. `createMonthlyStatementsV2` first will trigger start, only then produce the message.
> 
> * the start is idempotent so if already started, it won’t cause any harm
> * the distributed pubsub is at-most once tho, so it could still happen that maybe one of instance does not start… but I suppose this could be checked easily via logs or metrics.
> 
> ‌
> 
> We can also make this pause/resume status persisted, and check upon startup :thumbsup: 
> 
> ‌

**Conditions and limits:**

- Report may start TaskTopicSubscriber idempotently before producing in createMonthlyStatementsV2. Distributed pubsub is at-most-once and may miss an instance; logs/metrics can detect it. Persisted pause/resume is another option.
- PR title and inline path identify source component/operation context only; quoted PR title is metadata, not a claim that the comment proposal was implemented.

**Concern stated in the source:** We can extract amount validation into a method

```
  def validateAmountRestriction(maybeAmount: Option[BigDecimal], maybeRestriction: Option[SubscriptionAmountRegulation], context: String): Future[Done] = {
    maybeRestriction match {
      case Some(restriction) =>
        val expectedAmount = adjustAmount(maybeAmount, restriction)
        if (maybeAmount != expectedAmount) {
          Future.failed(BadRequest(s"$context breaches amount restrictions: request $maybeAmount, expected $expectedAmount"))
        } else {
          Future.successful(Done)
        }
      case None =>
        Future.successful(Done)
    }
  }
```

‌

And let caller decide how to extract amount \+ restriction, then handle Option themselves.

We can additionally create another method to extract amount for `PlanInvestmentBasedRequest` or `PlanUpsertInvestmentBasedRequest` if needed

>         if (maybeAmount != expectedAmount) {

## A2-1446 — package: Actually no need to split also right? This PR we will only release goal svc, all consumer of goal svc will still use old endpoints.

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 8568 ([EN-3050] Add initial funding instructions to plan models), goal-api/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/goal/api/requests/package.scala; original row 1446.

**Concern stated in the source:** Actually no need to split also right? This PR we will only release goal svc, all consumer of goal svc will still use old endpoints.

During release window, such request can hit either old or new goal instance

* old instance: continue working with V2, create cmd with amount but without fundingInstructions
* new instance: convert V2 to V3 request, create cmd with both amount and fundingInstructions

This cmd then again can hit either old or new goal instance

* old instance: create plan with amount but without fundingInstructions \(old behaviour\)
* new instance: create plan with both amount and fundingInstructions \(new behaviour\)

‌

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Actually no need to split also right? This PR we will only release goal svc, all consumer of goal svc will still use old endpoints.
>

> * old instance: continue working with V2, create cmd with amount but without fundingInstructions
> * new instance: convert V2 to V3 request, create cmd with both amount and fundingInstructions
> 
> This cmd then again can hit either old or new goal instance
> 
> * old instance: create plan with amount but without fundingInstructions \(old behaviour\)
> * new instance: create plan with both amount and fundingInstructions \(new behaviour\)
> 
> ‌

**Conditions and limits:**

## A2-1715 — AuroraJdbcSchema: Ah yes, creating them as empty is ok. My previous comment was in context of either the repository or the dbHandler having injected database.

**Source stance:** suggestion

**Context:**

> PR 7899 (PLATFORM-1097: Rebalance service pg readside migration), rebalance-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/rebalance/impl/db/AuroraJdbcSchema.scala; original row 1715.

**Concern stated in the source:** Ah yes, creating them as empty is ok. My previous comment was in context of either the repository or the dbHandler having injected database.

‌

Good examples:

```
_ <- database.run(someDbHandlerOrRepositoryInstanceWithoutInjectedDatabase.createTable)
_ <- database.run(SomeDbHandlerOrRepositoryCompanionObject.createTable)
```

In these cases, the Schema class with its injected database will decide where to create these tables. Hence we will create them in correct place \(even tho non-read-side ones will be empty cuz we haven’t migrated\)

‌

Potentially confusing example \(previous version of this PR\):

```
_ <- someDbHandlerOrRepositoryInstanceWithInjectedDatabase.createTable
```

Here, the injected database of Schema is ignored, and the dbHandler/repository will use its own injected database. And in this specific case, `rpcCommunicationDetailsJdbcRepository` and `planMarketValueJdbcHandler` both have only 1 instance using GCP jdbcDatabase.

‌

Either way, current PR looks good to me!

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Ah yes, creating them as empty is ok. My previous comment was in context of either the repository or the dbHandler having injected database.
> 
> ‌
> 
> Good examples:
> 
> ```
> _ <- database.run(someDbHandlerOrRepositoryInstanceWithoutInjectedDatabase.createTable)
> _ <- database.run(SomeDbHandlerOrRepositoryCompanionObject.createTable)
> ```
> 
> In these cases, the Schema class with its injected database will decide where to create these tables. Hence we will create them in correct place \(even tho non-read-side ones will be empty cuz we haven’t migrated\)
> 
> ‌
> 
> Potentially confusing example \(previous version of this PR\):
> 
> ```
> _ <- someDbHandlerOrRepositoryInstanceWithInjectedDatabase.createTable
> ```
> 
> Here, the injected database of Schema is ignored, and the dbHandler/repository will use its own injected database. And in this specific case, `rpcCommunicationDetailsJdbcRepository` and `planMarketValueJdbcHandler` both have only 1 instance using GCP jdbcDatabase.
> 
> ‌
> 
> Either way, current PR looks good to me!

**Conditions and limits:**

- The database controlling createTable matters: Schema.database.run(action) creates in chosen schema DB even if tables are empty, whereas child.createTable with injected DB silently targets child GCP. Current PR is accepted after that clarification.
- PR title and inline path identify source component/operation context only; quoted PR title is metadata, not a claim that the comment proposal was implemented.

## A3-0218 — Lagom/removed-Lagom error-serdes, shared breaker, whitelist and request-timeout verification matrix

**Source stance:** reported-verification

**Context:**

> None; PR: [INV-1974] feat(all-services): Consolidate svc exception serdes + circuit breaker config

**Concern stated in the source:** Able to return custom error json \(so that other services can deserialize\) instead of the default text response.

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> ## Test setup
> 
> instrument svc: Lagom-removed with test endpoint
> 
> * serialize error using ServiceErrorCompat
> * its client services deserialize error using `LagomCompatServiceExceptionSerializer`
> 
> ```
>   def testWater(testType: String): Future[Done] = {
>     testType match {
>       case "LagomBadRequest"  => Future.failed(lagomBadRequest("Invalid request"))
>       case "EndowusNotFound"  => Future.failed(apiNotFound("Entity id not found"))
>       case "SvcException"     => Future.failed(InstrumentSvcException("MorningStar down!", InstrumentSvcErrorType.MORNINGSTAR_API_CALL_FAILURE))
>       case "RuntimeException" => Future { Option.empty.get }
>       case "Slow"             => Future { Thread.sleep(20000) }.map(_ => Done)
>       case _                  => Future.successful(Done)
>     }
>   }
> ```
> 
> ```
> restCall(Method.GET, "/api/internal/instrument/test-water?testType", testWater _)
>     .withCircuitBreaker(CircuitBreaker.identifiedBy("shared-testing")),
> ```
> 
>  
> 
> marketdata svc: Lagom with test endpoint
> 
> * serialize error using `LagomServiceExceptionSerializer`
> * its client services also deserialize error using `LagomServiceExceptionSerializer`
> 
> ```
>   override def testWater(testType: String): ServiceCall[NotUsed, Done] = ServiceCall { _ =>
>     testType match {
>       case "LagomBadRequest"  => Future.failed(BadRequest("Invalid request"))
>       case "EndowusNotFound"  => Future.failed(NotFound("Entity id not found"))
>       case "SvcException"     => Future.failed(MarketDataSvcException("MAS down!", MarketDataSvcErrorType.MAS_MAINTENANCE))
>       case "RuntimeException" => Future { List.empty(1) }
>       case "Slow"             => Future { Thread.sleep(20000) }.map(_ => Done)
>       case _                  => Future.successful(Done)
>     }
>   }
> ```
> 
> ```
> restCall(Method.GET, "/api/internal/marketdata/test-water?testType", testWater _)
>     .withCircuitBreaker(CircuitBreaker.identifiedBy("shared-testing")),
> ```
> 
>  
> 
> goal svc: Lagom-removed with test endpoint calling either instrument / marketdata svc
> 
> * serialize error using ServiceErrorCompat
> 
> ```
>   def testWater(service: String, testType: String, handleSvcErr: Boolean): Future[Done] = {
>     service match {
>       case "marketdata" =>
>         marketDataService.testWater(testType).invoke().recover {
>           case e: MarketDataSvcException =>
>             if (handleSvcErr)
>               throw GoalSvcException("Something wrong with MarketData svc", GoalSvcErrorType.SOMETHING_WRONG)
>             else throw e
>         }
>       case "instrument" =>
>         instrumentService.testWater(testType).invoke().recover {
>           case e: InstrumentSvcException =>
>             if (handleSvcErr)
>               throw GoalSvcException("Something wrong with Instrument svc", GoalSvcErrorType.SOMETHING_WRONG)
>             else throw e
>         }
>       case _ => Future.successful(Done)
>     }
>   }
> ```
> 
>  
> 
> advisory svc: Lagom with test endpoint calling either instrument / marketdata svc
> 
> * serialize error using `LagomServiceExceptionSerializer`
> * also wrap 4xx to Lagom BadRequest to avoid error logging, but this is optional \(also not in scope of this PR\)
> 
> ```
>   override def testWater(service: String, testType: String, handleSvcErr: Boolean): ServiceCall[NotUsed, Done] = {
>     LagomExceptionWrappedServiceCall { _ =>
>       service match {
>         case "marketdata" =>
>           marketDataService.testWater(testType).invoke().recover {
>             case e: MarketDataSvcException =>
>               if (handleSvcErr)
>                 throw AdvisorySvcException("Something wrong with MarketData svc", AdvisorySvcErrorType.SOMETHING_WRONG)
>               else throw e
>           }
>         case "instrument" =>
>           instrumentService.testWater(testType).invoke().recover {
>             case e: InstrumentSvcException =>
>               if (handleSvcErr)
>                 throw AdvisorySvcException("Something wrong with Instrument svc", AdvisorySvcErrorType.SOMETHING_WRONG)
>               else throw e
>           }
>         case _ => Future.successful(Done)
>       }
>     }
> ```
> 
>  
> 
> instrument svc: Lagom-removed with test heavy endpoints
> 
> ```
>   def testHeavy: Future[Done] = {
>     Future { Thread.sleep(15000) }.map(_ => Done)
>   }
>   
>   Api.testHeavy impl { _ => testHeavy },
>   Api.testHeavyWithShortTimeout impl (_ => testHeavy, CustomTimeoutProcess(10.seconds)),
> ```
> 
> ## Test scenarios
> 
> Verified that error serdes works as expected \(as per `LagomServiceExceptionSerializerSpec` / `LagomCompatServiceExceptionSerializerSpec` / `ServiceErrorCompatSpec` \) for all combinations of:
> 
> * calling various testType in test endpoint of instrument/marketdata
> * calling various testType \+ option to handle underlying SvcException in test endpoint of advisory/goal \(forwarding to instrument/marketdata\)
> 
> Verified that if we use same `CircuitBreaker.identifiedBy("shared-testing")` in both instrument and marketdata endpoints, if one triggers circuit breaker, it will affect the other.
> 
> Verified that exception whitelist works as expected. No circuit breaker triggered for BadRequest/NotFound
> 
> Verified that endpoint specific request timeout works as expected. Able to return custom error json \(so that other services can deserialize\) instead of the default text response.

## A3-0515 — Post-Lagom API contract exception versus actor serializer; goal internal exception pattern unresolved

**Source stance:** explanation

**Context:**

> rebalance-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/rebalance/impl/entities/rebalancer/handlers/TriggerThresholdBreachedRebalanceCmdHandler.scala; PR: [INV-1303] feat(rebalance): Increase min backoff to 1.5s

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> Yeah this is where the voodoo happens.
> 
> 
> 
> Before:
> 
> * SvcException extends Lagom TransportException which the Lagom ExceptionSerializer knows how to serdes them. The `LagomServiceExceptionHelper` is extra logic to help avoiding sentry spamming
> * This same exception is also used to throw inside entity/cmdHandler. These can be serdes thanks to `JsonSerializer[AdvisorySvcException]`
> 
> 
> 
> After Lagom removal:
> 
> * SvcException in \*-api module are now intended as API contract only. They are converted to HTTP error via `EndpointResultCompat#mapToApiError`
> * akka serdes now is configured as
> 
> ```
> akka {
>   actor {
>     serializers {
>       play-json = "com.endowus.silver.persistence.serialization.PlayJsonSerializer"
>     }
>     serialization-bindings {
>       "akka.Done" = akka-misc
>       "akka.actor.Address" = akka-misc
>       "akka.remote.UniqueAddress" = akka-misc
>       "com.endowus.silver.persistence.serialization.PlayJsonSerializable" = play-json
>     }
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> * this is why if we want serdes to work… we need to extends `PlayJsonSerializable` \(all the state/cmd/evt do this\)
> * however, it’s debate-able whether we want to add this to our API contract. You can see none of the services do this, except for goal svc
> 
> 
> 
> Goal svc does it in a subtle way:
> 
> * it creates another `GoalSvcException` inside goal-impl and throw this in entity/cmdHandler
> * this is why serdes works for goal svc \(and only goal svc\)
> * and if such internal GoalSvcException is propagate to http, it converts back to the goal-api GoalSvcException
> 
> ```
>   val ServiceErrorMap: Throwable => Throwable = {
>     case logic.GoalSvcException(message, errorType) => GoalSvcException.toApiError(GoalSvcException(message, errorType))
>     case e: GoalSvcException                        => GoalSvcException.toApiError(e)
>     case e                                          => e
>   }
> ```
> 
> 
> 
> So following goal svc should work - but I’m not sure if this is the right way to do it. Let’s think more before we mass apply this pattern

**Conditions and limits:**

- Source wording is preserved in requested_change; interrogatives and proposals are not settled answers.
- The component path and PR title identify source context only; merged/resolved status is not evidence of implementation or correctness.
- The hunk evidence is source context; symbols or conditions found only there must not be attributed to the comment.
- Detailed before/after Lagom-removal serdes distinction retained. Goal internal GoalSvcException mapping is a possible model explicitly NOT approved for mass adoption.

## A3-0683 — StatusFields V1 bridge differs from always-present AssetTransfer units

**Source stance:** explanation

**Context:**

> transaction-api/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/transaction/api/models/TransactionTypes.scala; PR: [INV-1437] feat(transaction): Models

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> My rationale on not-using-StatusFields for this is:
> 
> * StatusFields is a bridge to V1 to support these optional-per-status fields, e.g. requestedAmount is None and only populated when transaction is created, settledAmount is None and only populated when transaction is settled etc
> * These fields are at top level in v1 TransactionDto, so the v2 to v1 mapping, we just blindly set them
> * Whereas in this AssetTransfer case, the field is required in v1 \(since we create dedicated v1 DTO for it\), and the value is always populated either with requestedUnits or settledUnits. This means `statusFields.requestedUnits` wouldn’t be used anywhere, but when it’s used for AssetTransfer, we will call `Option.get`. This is why it looks off in my head.

**Conditions and limits:**

- Source wording is preserved in requested_change; interrogatives and proposals are not settled answers.
- The component path and PR title identify source context only; merged/resolved status is not evidence of implementation or correctness.
- The hunk evidence is source context; symbols or conditions found only there must not be attributed to the comment.

> * assumed and confirmed order have amount and unit both required

## R-3538 — Final optional event fields defer optional-forever versus mandatory-plus-migration choice

**Source stance:** requested-change

**Context:**

> dividend-impl/src/main/scala/com/endowus/silver/dividend/impl/entities/dividend/ces/DividendEvents.scala; PR 2833: SILVER-11229: Fix settlement date for dividend reinvestment

**Source-preserving request, proposal, or question:**

> All new fields are now optional in events, hence all JsonMigration steps are removed.
> 
> We can:
> 
> A. Keep them optional forever to correctly reflect the event history, i.e. they are indeed new fields that were added at some point of time.
> 
> B. Make them mandatory \+ add back the migration step to provide default value in separate release
> 
> ‌
> 
> \(A\) would force new event processors to think and handle them, since all events will be re-processed by them. They might fallback to default values, or not. \(A\) give them an obligation to handle, but a choice to choose.
> 
> \(B\) effectively forces all new event processors to follow the default value via the serializer.
> 
> ‌
> 
> Making them optional now defer the decision of choosing \(A\) or \(B\) of out scope of this PR.

**Conditions and limits:**

- PR2833 preserves separate historical migration, Confirmed-only sync, date/timestamp meanings, and optional-field alternatives. Naming evolves through priceDate to settlementDate. The final comment defers optional-forever versus mandatory-plus-migration to a later decision.
